introduction: Michigan’s Food Assistance Program is SNAP. Apply and manage the case through MI Bridges; approved benefits use the Bridge Card.
description: Michigan’s Food Assistance Program is SNAP. Apply and manage the case through MI Bridges; approved benefits use the Bridge Card.

sections.who: MDHHS assesses household finances and applicable student, status and work rules. People living together who purchase and prepare food together generally form a household group.
sections.get: SNAP supplements grocery costs at approved retailers. The amount depends on the eligible household and calculation.
sections.docs:

sections.apply:
1. Apply through MI Bridges

    Use the application link on MDHHS Food Assistance.

  2. Complete follow-up

    Respond to interview and verification requests. Explain urgent food needs.

  3. Keep the account current

    Report required changes and read renewal tasks in MI Bridges.
sections.after: The state announces upgraded Bridge Cards later in 2026. Keep the mailing address current so replacement information reaches you.
sections.sources: Content checked October 1, 2026 using Michigan SNAP overview and application. Current eligibility and the final decision remain with the program.

faqs: The agency assesses income and other eligibility conditions; employment alone does not answer eligibility.
Where do I report a new address?
Use Report Changes in MI Bridges.
Do all adults face the same work rules?
No. Review current rules and exemptions with MDHHS.
Is the Bridge Card the application?
No. It is the benefit card issued after approval.
